q: Is the Pentagon preparing bases to run 90 days without power?
a: Partly. FORTRESS America is real: Hegseth signed the memo on September 30, 2026, and said every major base will make its own power. The 90-day figure comes from Fox News Digital, which reported it from internal documents. No public Pentagon document states 90 days yet, and Snopes lists that part as unverified.

A Department of War program created by a September 30, 2026 memo. It has five pillars: energy independence, supply chain resilience, a strategic defense reserve, installation hardening and cyber resilience, and resilience in space. The memo ordered a program office within 30 days. No budget or completion date has been published.

q: Did the UK tell people to stock up for 30 days?
a: No. The UK's Be Ready campaign, launched October 22, 2026, asks households to prepare for 3 days. The 30-day line came from Dan Bongino's podcast and then spread as UK advice.

q: What does the UK Be Ready campaign ask for?
a: Enough for 3 days without power, water, phones or internet: 3 litres of drinking water per person per day, food that needs no cooking, a torch, a power bank, a battery or wind-up radio, first aid, medicines, pet supplies and some cash.

q: Did Dan Bongino say to keep 30 days of food and water?
a: Yes. On his podcast on October 26, the former FBI deputy director told listeners to keep 30 days of food and water. He is not a government official, and no government source we found asks for 30 days.

q: Is the FEMA emergency alert test on November 17, 2026 real?
a: Yes. FEMA and the FCC scheduled a nationwide Emergency Alert System test for November 17, 2026, at about 2:20 pm Eastern on radio and TV, with December 3 as the backup date. Phones are not included and no action is needed. Federal law requires a test at least every three years; earlier ones ran in 2011, 2017, 2018 and 2023.

q: Did The Simpsons predict a blackout on November 17?
a: There is no evidence of that. The episode people cite, It's a Blunderful Life, aired on November 19, 2023 and shows no calendar date. The same claim went around for November 17, 2025, and nothing happened.

q: Why are governments telling people to stock up?
a: The governments themselves name power cuts, floods, cyberattacks, natural disasters and possible conflict. The UK, the EU and Japan ask for about 3 days, the standard household figure. Our analysis below finds the evidence fits a coordinated resilience push better than any single looming event, and says what would change that reading.
